newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE SHOWS NO SYMPATHY FOR FRENTZEN.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE SHOWS NO SYMPATHY FOR FRENTZEN.

text.p: World championship favourite Jacques Villeneuve showed his selfish streak on Thursday when he offered no sympathy for Williams team mate Heinz-Harald Frentzen's problems.
Frentzen is pointless after the opening two races in Australia and Brazil and he needs a solid result to boost his confidence in this Sunday's Argentine Grand Prix.

As the teams gathered in Buenos Aires for what will be the 600th world championship Grand Prix race since the inauguration of the series in 1950, Frentzen said he did not feel downcast and expected to be able to win for the Williams team this year.
"I am not making excuses," the German driver said. "But I have been here only six months and there is a lot to learn. Damon Hill was here for six years."

Villeneuve, who leads the world title race jointly with Briton David Coulthard, said: "We don't work together so I don't know what his problems are and I don't need to -- it's got nothing to do with me."
The Canadian lambasted the tight and twisty Oscar Galvez circuit as not being in "the spirit of Formula One," describing it as a high-speed kart track and comparing it to Monaco "without walls."
"I'm glad there are no other tracks like this one," he said. "When you hit a bump here, the pain can make you close your eyes."
On the day that the Williams team announced a one-year extension of their major sponsorship deal with Rothmans, Villeneuve also gave a salutory insight into how he feels the team works.

Speaking at a news conference on Thursday afternoon, he said: "It's a great team -- but it's a pragmatic team. You get in there and you do your work. That's it. But that's good. You are not in there to relax and to have a good time. You are there to work and to get results."
